overview: No server anticheat consumes the head-look packet: it carries only the head yaw byte, which plays no role in movement or combat verification. The corpus shows exactly two kinds of references: Artemis's packet-abstraction layer wraps the packet for its pipeline, and the NPC test rigs (PeyangSuperbAntiCheat, MinecraftAntiCheat) emit head rotations for fake players used to bait killaura. The packet is cosmetic clientbound state with no flag surface.

checks.name: GPacketPlayServerEntityHeadRotation (packet wrapper)
checks.purpose: Register the head-rotation packet in Artemis's packet abstraction layer so the pipeline can classify it; the read buffer is empty.
checks.how_it_works: The class is annotated with @PacketLink(PacketPlayServerEntityHeadRotation.class) and extends GPacket, binding the wrapper to the packet name; read() does nothing because no Artemis stage consumes the fields.
checks.variations: The same pattern appears for every play-state server packet in Artemis (entity, entity teleport, entity status, entity metadata).

checks.name: NPC head rotation (killaura test rig)
checks.purpose: Emit head-rotation packets for fake players so NPC bait looks alive while testing whether a player's aim tracks them.
checks.how_it_works: PeyangSuperbAntiCheat's NPCTeleport drives a fake EntityPlayer in a circle around the suspect (aura bot mode) or a panic radius (aura panic mode), sending PacketPlayOutEntityTeleport every tick plus PacketPlayOutEntityHeadRotation with the head yaw derived from the player's own head rotation. MinecraftAntiCheat's NPC utility sends the head-rotation packet through rotateHead alongside a look packet for any staff-created fake player.
checks.detects: Nothing by itself; the head rotation is part of the NPC bait that killaura checks observe from the attack side.
checks.variations: MinecraftAntiCheat builds the packet with raw field reflection (fields a and b) and always pairs it with PacketPlayOutEntityLook; PSAC computes the head yaw from the suspect's own rotation to make the NPC look at the target.
